## Citation

Hatle, K.M., Neveu, W., Dienz, O., Rymarchyk, S., Barrantes, R., Hale, S., Farley, N., Lounsbury, K.M., Bond, J.P., Taatjes, D.J., & Rincon, M. (2007). Methylation-Controlled J Protein Promotes c-Jun Degradation to Prevent ABCB1 Transporter Expression. *Molecular and Cellular Biology*, 27(8), 2952-2966.

## Abstract

The multidrug transporter ABCB1 is a major factor in drug resistance. This study reveals an epigenetic regulatory mechanism in which a methylation-controlled J protein promotes degradation of the c-Jun transcription factor, thereby suppressing ABCB1 expression.

## Key Findings

- Methylation state of a J protein regulates its interaction with proteasomal machinery
- The protein promotes ubiquitin-dependent degradation of c-Jun
- c-Jun suppression prevents activation of ABCB1 promoter
- Mechanism provides insight into epigenetic control of multidrug transporter expression

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed to molecular analysis and data interpretation.
